explanation: Track fuel as miles of remaining range. If a candidate start cannot reach the next city, no city in that failed segment can be a valid start, so restart after it. When a feasible tour exists, the final candidate is valid.
timeComplexity: O(n). One pass examines each city once.
spaceComplexity: O(1). Only a candidate index and constant-many fuel balances are retained.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: When the accumulated net range from a candidate start becomes negative, no city in that failed segment can be a valid start: a later start omits a nonnegative prefix and cannot repair that deficit. Restart after the failed segment. With the promised feasible total tour, the final candidate can complete the wraparound trip.
walkthrough: For gallons [1,0,2] and distances [25,10,25], the net ranges are -5,-10,+15 miles. The first two candidates fail, leaving start city 2. From city 2 the tank ranges are 15, then 10, then 0, so the full circuit succeeds. JSON arguments are [gallons,distances]. The callable returns a start index; expected true means the wrapper successfully simulated the complete trip from that returned index.
edgeCases: Tank capacity is unlimited and starts empty.
Several starts may be valid; any valid index is accepted.
The test contract supplies a nonempty feasible tour.
